labels.label: [6.N] normal forms through p = L(g) - id; the classes (prose, no environment)

hypotheses.paper: g an isometry, L(g) in SO0(1,n-1)
hypotheses.note: (∗), ker p = I^⊥ and tau mod I use only minkQ ∘ L(g) = minkQ and L(g) a linear equivalence (no determinant, no time orientation)

hypotheses.paper: hyperbolic: the boost matrix of rapidity ζ
hypotheses.note: reading ζ ≠ 0 (Barbot's matrix allows the identity)

hypotheses.paper: loxodromic R∘A, parabolic R∘A, factors isometries
hypotheses.note: factors required in lorentz d, as Barbot's R, A are elements of SO0(1,n-1)
reading U ≠ id (else every elliptic element is parabolic)

hypotheses.paper: 'Up to conjugacy, every isometry is of the following form' (l.1868): g ∈ Isom(𝐌ⁿ)
hypotheses.note: lorentz_trichotomy assumes exactly A ∈ lorentz d = SO₀(1,d) and is proved for every d, no dimension excluded; for d ≤ 1 the parabolic alternative is empty (two_le_of_unipotent)

findings: l.1852 (orig l.1828): 'p the element L(g)−id of SO₀(1,n−1)': p = L(g) − id is an endomorphism of 𝐌ⁿ (an element of the Lie algebra's ambient End(𝐌ⁿ)), not an element of SO₀(1,n−1); it is not even invertible unless L(g) has no fixed vector. Read 'p the endomorphism L(g) − id of 𝐌ⁿ' (pOf). The module docstring now quotes the sentence verbatim.

l.1875–1876 (orig l.1851–1852): 'I is spacelike, except if R is the identity map' — R is not defined in the elliptic item (it first appears at l.1894); read 'except if L(g) = id'. With spacelike meaning minkQ > 0 on I \ {0}, the exception is vacuous: I = 0 exactly when L(g) = id (range_pOf_eq_bot_iff), so the true statement is 'I is spacelike, and nonzero unless L(g) = id' (IsElliptic.range_spacelike).

l.1873 (orig l.1849): 'since M^n = I ⊕ I^⊥' is not justified; it holds for elliptic L(g) because Im p ∩ ker p = 0 (p y = x, p x = 0 make L(g)^k y = y + k x unbounded for the invariant norm) — IsElliptic.isCompl; it is false for unipotent L(g) ≠ id, where J = I ∩ I^⊥ ≠ 0.

l.1880–1887 (orig l.1856–1863): the hyperbolic matrix does not exclude ζ = 0 (the identity). Barbot's list is up to conjugacy and overlaps by design (hyperbolic ⊂ loxodromic, unipotent ⊂ parabolic), so overlap as such is not the defect; but with ζ = 0 allowed, every elliptic element is loxodromic (R∘id), so loxodromic ∩ elliptic ≠ ∅ and the trichotomy elliptic / loxodromic / parabolic is not a partition. ζ ≠ 0 is the reading that makes it one (IsLoxodromic.not_isElliptic).

l.1890 with l.1908 (orig l.1866, l.1884): 'Unipotent: p is nilpotent' includes L(g) = id, for which J = I ∩ I^⊥ = 0, contradicting 'J = I ∩ I^⊥ is a nontrivial isotropic space'. Strongest true form: under p ≠ 0, J is a null line (exists_mem_nullPart_ne_zero, nullPart_eq_span_of_mem); counterexample: any translation (p = 0).

l.1898–1899 vs l.1973–1974 (orig l.1874–1875, l.1949–1950): parabolic as listed (R elliptic, A unipotent, commuting) contains every elliptic element (A = id) and every unipotent one (R = id); §6.2 instead takes R non-trivial, which would exclude pure unipotents, while §7 (l.2085ff) treats id + p as parabolic. Formalized: U ≠ id, R any elliptic; then the classes are pairwise disjoint (proved).

l.1943–1951 (orig l.1919–1927): 'L(g) is then represented, in a non-orthogonal frame, by the matrix' — the displayed matrix (p v1 = v0, p vn = v1, zero elsewhere) is the matrix of p = L(g) − id, not of L(g) (unipotent_frame).

l.1929–1931 (orig l.1905–1907): 'v1' = p(vn) is a non-trivial element of I \ J' is asserted without argument; it follows from (∗) at (vn, vn): if p vn = c v0 then 2c⟨vn|v0⟩ = 0, so p vn = 0, i.e. vn ∈ I^⊥, which is orthogonal to v0. Gap filled, not an error.

l.1985–1989 (orig l.1961–1965): the R-invariant vn is obtained through an R-invariant euclidean orthogonal of J^⊥; an alternative needing no euclidean norm: otherwise v0 ∈ (𝓘^⊥)^⊥ = 𝓘, and 𝓘 ∩ 𝓘^⊥ = 0 for elliptic R (parabolic_exists_fixed_not_mem).

l.2008–2014 (orig l.1984–1990): 'the linear case if τ belongs to I' is meaningful only after the normalisation τ ∈ 𝓘^⊥, since τ is defined modulo I ⊕ 𝓘 (l.2001), not modulo I; as an invariant of g it reads τ ∈ Im(L(g) − id), i.e. g has a fixed point (IsLinearCase, exists_fixed_iff, parabolic_mem_range_iff).
questions: IsHyperbolic: is the rapidity meant to be nonzero (reading taken: ζ ≠ 0)?
IsParabolic: U ≠ id and R arbitrary elliptic (reading taken), or R non-trivial as in §6.2 l.1974?

The tangent/transverse cases are defined relative to the unipotent factor U (J = J(U)); for a parabolic g this presumes the decomposition L(g) = R∘U is unique, which is true (Jordan–Chevalley) but not proved here. Should J be defined intrinsically (the fixed null line of L(g))?

'Preserves some euclidean norm' is read as: preserves a symmetric positive definite bilinear form; it is proved equivalent, in SO0(1,d), to fixing a future timelike vector (isElliptic_iff_exists_fixed_timelike).

labels.label: [6.U] unipotent linear parts, with Rem 6.1 (prose)

hypotheses.note: plus p ≠ 0, which 'J nontrivial' (l.1908) needs; DEC-27 strongest true form, counterexample p = 0

findings: see [6.N]: J nontrivial needs p ≠ 0 (l.1908); the frame matrix is that of p (l.1943); I \ J gap at l.1929–1931 filled. Proved additionally: p³ = 0, dim I = 2, dim J = 1, dim J^⊥ = d, J^⊥ = I + I^⊥ (used without proof at l.1961). Barbot's p̄ = 0 on J^⊥/J (l.1912–1916) is proved by a descent on (∗) rather than through the quotient norm.

Counterexample stated in Lean: L(g) = id is unipotent (isUnipotent_one) and nullPart 1 = ⊥ (nullPart_one), so 'J = I ∩ I^⊥ is a nontrivial isotropic space' (l.1908) fails for p = 0. Moreover a nontrivial unipotent forces n ≥ 3 (two_le_of_unipotent): for n = 2 the unipotent class is {id}.

labels.label: [6.P] parabolic linear parts (prose)

hypotheses.note: R any elliptic element of SO0(1,d), so the unipotent case R = id is covered

findings: see [6.N]: the linear case 'τ ∈ I' (l.2010) is a normal-form statement; as a class it is τ ∈ Im(L(g) − id). The final claim (l.2016–2017) is proved for every affine subspace with direction J^⊥ (parabolic_not_transverse_iff), from a general criterion transPart_mem_iff_map_eq.

kb_proposals: minkB-orthogonals: use minkOrth W := (minkForm d).orthogonal W (Flat/Isometries); membership unfolds to IsOrtho, so a rw by minkB lemmas fails on `hx w hw` until restated as `have : minkB w x = 0 := hx w hw` (or `show minkB _ _ = 0`).
Destructuring `x ∈ W ⊓ W'` with rintro yields coerced memberships `x ∈ ↑W`; re-ascribe (`have h : x ∈ W := h`) before `rw [LinearMap.mem_ker]`.

A Brouwer-free fixed point in H^d for an elliptic Lorentz map: minimise the invariant euclidean norm on the future unit hyperboloid; the minimiser is unique by reverse Cauchy–Schwarz and strict convexity (IsElliptic.exists_fixed_timelike). The trichotomy's cone eigenvector is variational too (lorentz.exists_null_eigen_or_fixed_timelike).

Linear-algebra facts about Lorentz maps reduce to two tools: (∗) and 'two orthogonal null vectors are proportional' (eq_smul_of_null_orth); eigenvalue arguments go through eigen_line (eigenvalue l with l² ≠ 1 gives a null line).

Determinant 1 for a Lorentz map without computing it: if A = B ∘ B with B minkQ-preserving, det A = (det B)² ≥ 0 and det A² = 1 (Gram matrix: LinearMap.toMatrix₂_compl₁₂ + LinearMap.nondegenerate_iff_det_ne_zero, import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Matrix.SesquilinearForm), so det A = 1; one-parameter families (boostLin_comp, nullRotLin_comp) give the square root (Flat/Isometries det_eq_one_of_eq_sq).

A Brouwer-free cone eigenvector for A ∈ SO₀(1,d): if A has no null eigenvector, ⟨Ax|x⟩ < 0 on the closed future cone, so x ↦ |x|²/⟨Ax|x⟩ attains its max on the compact section {x₀ = 1} at a timelike v; the first variation (IsLocalMin.hasDerivAt_eq_zero on t ↦ F(v + t w), a quadratic) gives 2v = m(Av + A⁻¹v), an invariant plane (Flat/Isometries lorentz.exists_null_eigen_or_fixed_timelike).

Splitting an isometry along an eigenvalue without Jordan–Chevalley uniqueness: mathlib's Fitting decomposition LinearMap.eventually_isCompl_ker_pow_range_pow (p = A − id) plus orthogonality from the adjoint identity ⟨x | p z⟩ = −⟨A⁻¹ p x | z⟩, induction on the power; the factor 'A on ker pᴺ, id on Im pᴺ' is LinearMap.ofIsCompl, made an equivalence by LinearEquiv.ofInjectiveEndo (injective because it preserves minkQ) (Flat/Isometries isElliptic_or_isParabolic_of_null_fixed).
In a long proof, `set e := c • w` lets `rw [minkB_smul_left]` rewrite inside e's body (it unifies through the let); introduce opaque names with `obtain ⟨e, he⟩ : ∃ e, e = c • w := ⟨_, rfl⟩` instead.
